# EDR: Agile Manifesto — what agile is, as the repository reads it

## Rules: EDR-AGILE

Each rule is one reading of the manifesto's claim about what agile is. Every source line names the manifesto page; the sentence is the
repository's own summary, never a quotation.

### Rule EDR-AGILE-DEFINEDBYMANIFESTO

Agile is defined by the manifesto's four values ([EDR-VALUES](agile-values.md)) and twelve principles
([EDR-AGILEPRINCIPLES](agile-principles.md)), not by any framework, ceremony, role, or tool.

Source: [Manifesto for Agile Software Development](https://agilemanifesto.org) (2001)

Binds to [WDR-KAIZEN-AGILEFROMMANIFESTO](../../process/inspect-and-adapt.md#rule-wdr-kaizen-agilefrommanifesto).

### Rule EDR-AGILE-RESPONDTOCHANGE

Every value and principle serves one capacity: to alter direction quickly and cheaply as understanding grows. A process that makes change
expensive is not agile, whatever it is called.

Source: [Manifesto for Agile Software Development](https://agilemanifesto.org) (2001)

Binds to [WDR-KAIZEN-AGILEFROMMANIFESTO](../../process/inspect-and-adapt.md#rule-wdr-kaizen-agilefrommanifesto).

### Rule EDR-AGILE-VALUESOVERFRAMEWORKS

A framework (Scrum, Kanban, XP) is one implementation of the values and principles; the manifesto is the source, so when a practice
contradicts a value, the practice changes.

Source: [Manifesto for Agile Software Development](https://agilemanifesto.org) (2001)

Binds to [WDR-KAIZEN-AGILEFROMMANIFESTO](../../process/inspect-and-adapt.md#rule-wdr-kaizen-agilefrommanifesto).

### Rule EDR-AGILE-PROVENBYOUTCOMES

The manifesto prizes working software and responding to change over process and plans, so agility shows in outcomes (software delivered
frequently, direction changed cheaply), not in following every ceremony.

Source: [Manifesto for Agile Software Development](https://agilemanifesto.org) (2001)

Binds to [WDR-KAIZEN-AGILEFROMMANIFESTO](../../process/inspect-and-adapt.md#rule-wdr-kaizen-agilefrommanifesto) and
[PDR-NOWASTE-DROPUNNEEDEDSTEPS](../../principles/reduce-waste.md#rule-pdr-nowaste-dropunneededsteps).

## Context

"Agile" is among the most overloaded words in software: it names a manifesto, a family of frameworks, a certification industry, and a
management style. The Agile Manifesto, written in 2001 by seventeen practitioners meeting at Snowbird, Utah, is the one short, comparative
statement they agreed on. The manifesto text is published on its own site; this record summarises it and quotes nothing beyond the names of
the values.
